text:
alex: FYI saw a spike of metadata verification errors on local NVMe across some eu-west2-g hosts during the 03:20 batch window. GPUs failing to attach, kube pods stuck Pending. logs pasted below.

mike: can you paste the alert or grafana link?

alex: https://grafana.internal/d/host/ephemeral-iowait?panel=12 — high iowait, blk_rq_issue errors. sample from node gnode-eu-west2-47:
```
[ 1623.421234] nvme nvme0: Completing unknown admin cmd op: 0x1
[ 1623.421237] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 4096
[ 1623.421240] EXT4-fs (nvme0n1p1): error count since last fsck: 5
```

sylvia: ugh. how many nodes impacted?

alex: currently ~12 hosts spread across two racks, all same SSD SKU (PM1733-ish). Most show elevated scrub throughput and increased metadata checksum failures in our overlayfs layer.

lina: any correlation with the batch scheduler? did we push a new janitor/scrubber config?

alex: yes, the batch rollout at 03:15 increased concurrent small-block writes. scrubber run overlap + aggressive fstrim we rolled out last week — looks like write amplification + sudden GC on drives.

frank: immediate mitigation: cordon affected nodes and drain non-critical pods. we should also pause the janitor/scrub for that rack and scale down batch concurrency.

mike: agreed. I'm starting an automated cordon+drain for the 12 nodes now. ops-bot: run playbook nvme-isolation-2026.

ops-bot: playbook started: nvme-isolation-2026. Steps: cordon -> drain -> redeploy pods to eu-west2-b/c -> disable janitor for 1h -> run smartctl snapshot -> notify storage team.

storage-bot: smartctl snapshot for gnode-eu-west2-47: "SMART overall-health self-assessment test result: FAILED"; nvme error log shows 120 media errors in past 48h.

lina: if SMART is failing we should plan replacement, but first confirm if remount+fsck fixes transient corruption. frank any fsck guidance?

frank: run readonly mount, copy out KV caches if present, then unmount and fsck with -f -c. But avoid mass fsck during batch window — do one node at a time. Also run nvme-cli fw-log to check firmware hiccups.

alex: doing a rolling procedure: 1) cordon 1 node 2) migrate GPU workloads to spare pool 3) snapshot ephemeral caches where possible 4) unmount and fsck 5) run scrub in controlled mode 6) bring back.

mike: note: migrating GPUs will increase on-demand Dedicated spend if spares are on dedicated hosts. Cost estimate: ~12 nodes * 0.9 GPU-hours extra ~ ~$1500 over 24h if sustained. we should weigh replacement vs transient fix.

sylvia: short-term: reduce batch concurrency to 30% and backoff janitor schedules. medium-term: schedule vendor RMA for affected SKU and consider moving next batch window to eu-west2-b/c only.

lina: also add temp heuristic: if media errors > 50 and iowait > 40% mark node as 'nvme-degraded' to avoid auto-provisioning new GPU attaches.

frank: good. i'll open a CR to add that gate to provisioning policy and an alert to escalate earlier.

alex: long-term postmortem TODO: quantify write amplification from our overlayfs+fstrim combo, consider changing fstrim interval and scrub sampler thresholds. Also consider replication of ephemeral caches to avoid fsck restores.

mike: are we comfortable with the rolling plan? approve?

sylvia: approve — proceed with cordon+drain now. update channel as nodes finish.

ops-bot: cordon+drain completed for 3/12 nodes, 9 remaining.

alex: I'll post final log snippets after the first fsck completes. thanks all :thumbsup:
